stimulus.text:
Abigail Adams to John Adams, March 31, 1776:

“I long to hear that you have declared an independency. I desire you would remember the ladies and be more generous and favourable to them than your ancestors. Do not put such unlimited power into the hands of the husbands. Remember, all men would be tyrants if they could. If particular care and attention is not paid to the ladies, we are determined to foment a rebellion, and will not hold ourselves bound by any laws in which we have no voice or representation.”
stimulus.source_note: Abigail Adams to John Adams, March 31, 1776. Founders Online, National Archives. Public domain.

rationales.B: Republican motherhood gave women a civic duty, raising virtuous citizens, while Adams asked for fairer laws and a voice.
rationales.A: Republican motherhood claimed no vote or office for women.
rationales.C: Republican motherhood argued women needed education to teach their sons.
rationales.D: Republican motherhood kept women at home; it did not send them into trade or farming.
rationales.general:
1. The letter asks for laws more generous to women and limits on husbands’ power.
2. Background: republican motherhood, as the books describe it, gave women the civic task of raising civic-minded sons and shaping men’s morals.
3. Background: it claimed no political equality and no vote or office for women.
4. So it differed by offering a domestic civic role instead of the legal equality Adams sought.
Remember: a new idea can give a group importance without giving it equal rights.
